4.text: Exposing of the Body. — On arriving at the place indicated by divina-

5.text: tion, the people choose some level spot for the funeral, and, laying off on it a

6.text: portion about the size of the body, they encircle it with stones in the form of

7.text: an elongated oval. (Plate XXXIV, Figs 1, 2). One end of the oval is pointed

8.text: toward midnight, and the opposite end is left partly open. This enclosure of

9.text: stones is called “enclosure of the dead one” (palaˊwkun). Sometimes three stones

10.text: are considered sufficient to form the enclosure. One is placed near the head

11.text: of the corpse, and the other two, one near each shoulder. In this case

12.text: the stones selected must be larger than usual. When stones are scarce, as

13.text: in the interior and far from the river-banks, the enclosure may be formed of

14.text: three short logs, laid out in the same order as the three big stones of the

16.text: The sledge with the corpse is pointed with its head toward midnight.

17.text: Then the reindeer are unhitched, and with four knives they are stabbed

18.text: simultaneously from the right and from the left side. As soon as they have

19.text: fallen, the harness is put on again; but the collars are now placed over the

20.text: right shoulder, the reverse of the usual way. The chief of the cortège, sitting

21.text: in his place astride of the corpse, jerks the reins violently, and urges the

22.text: reindeer with the whip, pretending that he is going fast to the country of

23.text: the dead. The other people encourage him, exclaiming, “Hurry up! go

24.text: faster!” When the slaughtered reindeer kick about in the last agonies, the

25.text: people exclaim, “Oh, they are going fast!” The chief of the cortège says,

30.text: The harness is taken off the dead reindeer, the corpse is lifted from the

31.text: sledge, and put, still all wound up with thong, upon the ground within the

32.text: “enclosure of the dead one.” Its head is pointed toward midnight. The

33.text: place has been previously strewn with bits of tallow and sausage brought

34.text: for that purpose. The reindeer are skinned, and their meat is cut off in

35.text: large, thin slices. The bones of the legs are broken with an adze, and the

36.text: antlers chopped off together with the top of the crown. Two tent-poles are

37.text: placed on the ground near the feet of the corpse, pointed in the direction of

38.text: its legs. These poles are its wooden legs, to be employed in the country

39.text: of the dead. Usually they are the same poles that were laid under the

40.text: runners of the sledge, near the entrance, at the time of divination. In

41.text: case of necessity, the tent-poles may be replaced by long sticks cut off in the

42.text: woods. Then several of the “followers” approach the corpse and proceed to
